recommendation: Keep this source fix. It removes a stale contradiction in the built Goal definition without changing the already-applied cardinality or expanding the scope beyond FHIR-12776.
issue_request: FHIR-12776 was a Published/Persuasive Patient Care change request for FHIR-core Goal. It rejected using omitted Goal.subject as an anonymization mechanism and resolved that Goal.subject should be changed to 1..1.
initial_application: The April 2017 application commit 25735dcc63a312d77a995ab0d2d8d0ab2ed7f835 changed the then-authoritative Goal spreadsheet cardinality for Goal.subject from 0..1 to 1..1 and added a committee note tying the change to GF#12776. Later source migrations preserved the 1..1 cardinality in source/goal/structuredefinition-Goal.xml.
additional_context: The current Goal resource is active in source/fhir.ini, so source/goal/structuredefinition-Goal.xml feeds the current build. The current element still carried requirements text saying subject was optional for anonymized reporting, which contradicted both the current 1..1 cardinality and FHIR-12776's rationale. No Zulip or Confluence evidence was found that changed the Jira/source conclusion.
reconciliation: Updated Goal.subject requirements text in the active StructureDefinition source to explain why a Goal needs to preserve its subject, including in anonymized reporting, while leaving the already-correct 1..1 cardinality unchanged.
source_changes: source/goal/structuredefinition-Goal.xml: replaced the stale Goal.subject requirements text that said subject was optional for anonymized reporting with text aligned to the required subject decision.

evidence_items.summary: Goal is listed as an active resource and Goal.subject currently has min=1 and max=1.
